correctness.rationale: On each finite open arclength regime, both endpoint motions are affine with unit tangents u,v. The arc-and-chord shoelace expression has quadratic coefficient [v,u]/2: among the changing terms only the closing chord determinant is quadratic. Differentiation gives 2B'=[q-p,u+v] and B''=-[u,v]. Distinct parallel edge directions are opposite in the stated convex-vertex setting, yielding constant area; nonparallel tangents yield a true quadratic. No endpoint pair lies in one edge because each edge is shorter than half the perimeter. Splitting nonconstant regimes at derivative zeros and B=V/2 produces finitely many monotone inverse-square-root pushforwards, while constant intervals give length/P and only a finite null set is omitted. On bases b>a, arclength matching yields upper abscissa xi+C-t with C=(a+b+c-d)/2, and |c-d|<b-a implies that the entire (C-a,C) interval lies inside the long base. Its cap is h(a+b-C)/2, out of V=h(a+b)/2. The reverse-oriented interval supplies the complement and the same smaller fraction, giving exactly one atom of mass 2a/P and location 1/2-|c-d|/(2(a+b)); equal legs give the isosceles case. A parallelogram's central reflection is the half-perimeter shift and bisects area for every chord. No opposite parallels means no constant regime. Independent rational arclength partition and shoelace samples, including a horizontally offset trapezoid absent from the frozen test, recover atoms (location,mass) = (4/9,7/23) and (1/2,7/25).
residual_risks: Finite exact examples corroborate rather than establish the law. Polygon density proof uses nonredundant strictly convex vertices; a convention allowing a collinear extra vertex in a quadrilateral merely presents a triangle, with no opposite parallel sides or atom.
